# Reviewed gitleaks allowlist exceptions for this repository.
#
# The secret-scan workflow builds its gitleaks configuration itself: the pinned, vendored
# ruleset in this directory, plus whatever rules .gitleaks.toml ADDS, re-emitted field by
# field. A repository allowlist is never carried into that configuration, so it cannot
# subtract anything from the scan -- read that twice, because it is the opposite of what
# a file called "exceptions" usually means:
#
#   Listing a digest here does NOT make the scan ignore anything. It only says that this
#   allowlist has been read and may exist in .gitleaks.toml -- for gitleaks run locally,
#   or by an editor plugin -- without failing CI. Verified: with the digest below's
#   allowlist approved, the config gate passed and the scan still reported the planted
#   credential and failed the job.
#
# Without an entry here, any allowlist in .gitleaks.toml fails the job outright, because
# an unreviewed allowlist in the repository is how three of the four ways to make this
# scan lie began.
#
# Format: one lowercase sha256 digest per line, optionally followed by "# why".
# The digest is over the canonical JSON of the allowlist table, sorted by key, with no
# whitespace -- the workflow prints the digest of any allowlist it rejects, so adding an
# exception is: read the allowlist in the diff, decide it may exist, paste the digest here
# IN THE SAME REVIEW, and say why on the line.
#
# An allowlist attached to a rule ([rules.allowlist]) is rejected whatever is listed here:
# the gate cannot re-emit that field, so it refuses the rule rather than guessing.
#
# There are none today.
